cases.family: overclaim relative to a stated comparison
cases.original_value: the data generated by our method achieves the best results in 18.
cases.injected_value: the data generated by our method achieves the best results in all 21.
cases.surrounding_original: Among the 21 metrics, the data generated by our method achieves the best results in 18. From the last row of the table, it can be observed that...
cases.why_inconsistent: The paper's own preceding clause states the comparison is over 21 metrics and the original sentence honestly reports winning 18 of them. The injected wording claims a sweep of all 21, strengthening a bounded, already-stated comparison ratio into an unqualified superlative the same paragraph's own numbers do not support.

cases.original_value: All settings are exactly the same as LDReg except for the regularization term.
cases.surrounding_original: All results are based on 100 epoch pretraining with BYOL and ResNet-50. All settings are exactly the same as LDReg except for the regularization term. Table 16: The linear evaluation results on comparing different regularization terms.
cases.why_inconsistent: This sentence is the paper's own statement that Table 16's regularization-term comparison varies exactly one thing. Deleting it leaves Table 16's comparison with no stated control: a reader can no longer tell, from the surrounding text alone, whether anything besides the regularization term differs between the compared runs.

cases.original_value: The regularization hyperparameter λ is set at 1.
cases.surrounding_original: We use three eigenvectors (k = 3) for our representative subspace. The regularization hyperparameter λ is set at 1. Additionally, the hyperparameters α and β control the degree of complementarity and similarity in our optimization equation.
cases.why_inconsistent: λ weights the regularization term in the paper's own optimization objective (Section 18's Eq.) and the results section's reported numbers depend on its value. Deleting the one sentence that states λ=1 leaves that dependency unspecified in the experimental-setup section, while the claim built on it is unchanged.

cases.source_paper_title: Is Score Matching Suitable for Estimating Point Process Parameters
cases.surrounding_original: In Table 1, we report the MAE of parameter estimates for three models trained by MLE, (A)SM, and (A)WSM on the synthetic dataset.
cases.why_inconsistent: Table 1 (table_idx 0) reports MAE on the synthetic dataset -- exactly what this sentence describes. Table 2 (table_idx 1) reports TLL and ACC for a different model class (attention-based deep Hawkes processes) and contains no MAE-on-synthetic-dataset figures at all, so redirecting the citation points the claim at a table that cannot contain the cited quantity.
